task: Implement the global lifecycle control plane so Proofbound hosts can inspect runtime closure, proof-consumption closure, queue governance, dashboard state, and named guardrails from mechanical CLI output.
outcome: After the story is done, an operator can run lattice global_control_status --format=json and see story rows with authoritativeCwd, runtime status, consumption status, queue classification, nextSafeAction, Tier-C experiment grouping, duplicate cleanup suggestions, and explicit local-only proof boundaries without stitching session_brief, story_authority_resolve, lifecycle_check, and stale plan docs.
facts: B-376c completed schema and milestone alignment only; it deliberately did not implement full CP-0 through CP-5 behavior.
Existing lifecycle-control modules currently expose status shapes and read-only compatibility helpers, not registered commands or real projectors.

story_authority_resolve, lifecycle_check, done_closure, Proof Admissibility, owner lease, main write lock, validation lock, and evidence freshness modules already exist and should remain sources of truth.
INIT reviewers passed with advisories requiring explicit product-visible completion criteria and strict non-replacement of lifecycle/proof/Authority semantics.
constraints: Do not create a second lifecycle state machine or bypass story_advance gates.
Do not reimplement Proof Admissibility policy, evidence freshness classification, DONE oracle, or Evidence Runtime verification.
Do not optimize arbitrarily; only implement the real correctness and consistency gaps named by the execution plan.
Keep Authority/production semantics out of the control plane; render lower-layer results only.
Queue exceptions must preserve Tier-C experiment evidence and must not hide malformed or cleanup-required stories.
All user-facing CLI output must separate story-level blockers from project-level queue health.
unknowns: Which existing public APIs expose enough proof-admissibility waterline detail for CP-2 without adding a competing schema?
